column1: # The format is described in src/legacy/table.rs. Codes are Windows-1252 bytes.
# Derived from documents, as no code page is published. The glyphs were rendered
# from the Shree-Kan-0850 TrueType font (version 1.0 of 18 March 2000) that the
# Udayavani newspaper served to readers of its web pages as
# (capture of 10 April 2003). Each glyph was identified by eye and matched against
# glyphs shaped with HarfBuzz from Noto Sans Kannada, then checked in context: the
# Kannada text of 173 Udayavani story pages archived in 2003 and 2004, which name
# Shree-Kan-0850 in their font tags, was converted, and every unknown glyph and
# malformed syllable was read against the same text rendered in the font.
# docs/shree-lipi.md has the method and results.
# Codes the font has but no page used are left out, and are reported as unknown,
# except those at ASCII punctuation codes, which pass through as punctuation: 23 (ಓಂ),
# 5D, 5F, 60 and 7D draw Kannada glyphs no page used.
# Consonants drawn without the head stroke
# Consonants built from 2 to 4 glyphs: ಮ from ವ, ಝ from ರ, ಯ from bases of its own.
# E1 is their tail, DE the tail with ಾ, E5 the tail before the virama.
# Vowel signs. DC is the head stroke for the inherent a.
# Typists put the wide blank 24 before a subscript or ೖ to move it right, and write
# ಾ with ೖ for ೈ in names such as ಶಾಂಘೈ.
# Spacing glyphs with no text value. 2D draws nothing; typists used 26 for the hyphen.
# 24 draws a wide blank, typed only to move the next glyph.
# Punctuation drawn at codes ASCII uses for others. 3E draws a short bar, typed after
# abbreviations and numbers, as in ಸಂ।ರದ.
